questions.stem: The metabolic reactions involving phosphate group transfer by kinase enzymes are important flux-controlling reactions in a pathway and are generally irreversible. Which of the following kinase reaction is reversible?
questions.solutionHtml:
Phosphoglycerate Kinase
  • Transfers phosphoryl group from substrate 1,3 Bis phosphoglycerate to ADP to form ATP and 3-phosphoglycerate
  • First substrate-level phosphorylation reaction of glycolysis
  • A reversible reaction is the phosphorylation of 3-phosphoglycerate to 1,3 Bis phosphoglycerate by using ATP during gluconeogenesis.
  • The name of the enzyme is given to fit for this reaction

Other reversible kinase reactions are:

  • Creatine kinase
  • Succinate thiokinase

questions.stem: Which of the following is commonly used in blood collection vials for glucose estimation?A. NaFB. CitrateC. HeparinD. Potassium oxalateE. Clot ActivatorSelect the correct answer from given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
A, D

Blood collection vials

  • Grey colored cap vials
  • Contains sodium fluoride (NaF) and potassium oxalate (1:3 mixture).
  • NaF inhibits glycolysis in blood cells, by inhibiting the enzyme enolase.
  • Potassium oxalate serves as an anticoagulation agent
  • It helps in the accurate estimation of glucose even if the sample is stored for a longer time.

questions.stem: ATP/ADP acts as a sensor of the energy status of the cells and acts by binding as an allosteric regulator to the regulatory enzymes. ATP is an allosteric regulator of which of the following enzyme?
questions.solutionHtml:
PFK 1 and Pyruvate kinase
  • PFK-1 is the RLE of glycolysis with ATP as its substrate
  • Pyruvate kinase is the last enzyme of glycolysis and produces ATP by SLP
  • Excess of ATP in the cell (energy-rich state) will inhibit both enzymes using allosteric inhibition to stop glycolysis.
  • Fructose 2,6-bisphosphate and Fructose 1,6-bisphosphate are allosteric activators of PFK-1 and Pyruvate kinase respectively.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No.184

questions.stem: ATP produced via substrate-level phosphorylation in glycolysis is:
questions.solutionHtml:
4

Substrate-level phosphorylation refers to the formation of ATP when a phosphoryl group is transferred from a high energy compound directly to ADP. There are two substrate-level phosphorylation steps in glycolysis which form a total of 4 ATP per glucose molecule. 

ATP yield via substrate-level phosphorylation in glycolysis is 4 ATPs

  • There are 2 (SLP) steps in glycolysis:
    • Phosphoglycerate kinase (Step - 7)
    • Pyruvate kinase (Step- 10)
  • These steps occur in phase II of glycolysis.
  • The number of ATPs produced are multiplied by 2 (as two molecules of Glyceraldehyde-3-P enters Phase II),
  • e. total 2+2 = 4 ATPs/glucose



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 164

questions.stem: Pyruvate can be converted directly into all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
Phosphoenol Pyruvate
  • Pyruvate to PEP conversion is required for the process of gluconeogenesis.
  • The reverse process i.e. PEP to pyruvate conversion happens in glycolysis and it is catalyzed by pyruvate kinase.
    • However, it is an irreversible step due to large negative ΔG.
    • So, pyruvate can't be converted directly into PEP.
  • Pyruvate to PEP conversion during gluconeogenesis occurs indirectly in two steps:
    • first conversion of pyruvate to OAA using the enzyme pyruvate carboxylase
    • then OAA conversion to PEP by PEP carboxykinase.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 167

questions.stemHtml: This pathway is occurring in which cell of the body:
questions.solutionHtml:
RBCs
  • This is RL shunt i.e. Rapaport Leubering shunt/ cycle which occurs only in RBCs
  • Out of all the glucose entering the RBCs, 10% goes through the RL shunt.
  • In RL shunt, substrate level phosphorylation (SLP) step by phosphoglycerate kinase enzyme does not occur. So, the net gain of ATP is zero.
  • RL shunt is important for the production of 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate (2,3 BPG)
  • This compound is required in RBCs to release oxygen from HbA at the tissue level.


Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 168

questions.stem: Which among the following is the true statement(s) regarding Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) deficiency?A. Fumarate level increasesB. Exercise intoleranceC. Muscle cramps may occurD. lactate dehydrogenase operates in anaerobic conditionE. It is a key enzyme in Kreb's cycleSelect the correct answer from given below code
questions.solutionHtml:
B, C, D

Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)

  • Works under anaerobic conditions
  • Converts pyruvate to lactate by oxidation and regenerates NAD from NADH
  • This enzyme is normally required during exercise as there is low availability of O2 during strenuous exercise and cells mostly obtain energy by anaerobic conversion of glucose to lactate.
  • So, the deficiency of LDH will lead to low energy production in muscle during exercise causing exercise intolerance & muscle cramps due to lactate accumulation.
  • After the exercise, the lactate is again converted back to pyruvate relieving the muscle cramps in Cori’s cycle.
  • But in the case of LDH def, lactate will remain for a longer time causing sustained muscle cramps.

questions.stem: In the absence or shortage of oxygen certain cells or tissue resort to anaerobic glycolysis. The end product of anaerobic glycolysis are:
questions.solutionHtml:
2 ATP + 2 NAD

Anaerobic Glycolysis

  • ETC is not working hence NADH cannot enter ETC to form ATP.
  • NADH is used to regenerate NAD by LDH
  • Lactate is a dead end as it cannot be further metabolized under anaerobic conditions.
  • So, 2 Lactate and 2 NAD are end products of anaerobic glycolysis.
  • Net gain of ATP:
    • 4 ATP produced (substrate level phosphorylation) – 2 ATP used (one by Hexokinase, other used by PFK-1) = 2 ATP (net gain).
  • Here, they are asking about the end-product, and at the end of anaerobic glycolysis, 2 ATP and 2 NAD are obtained.
  • So, when asked about end-product then you have to mark 2ATP + 2NAD.

questions.stem: Person of age 23 years was employed on the horticulture farm where he performed pesticide spray on the plants. Accidentally, he inhaled pesticide spray and was taken to the hospital with restlessness, seizure, vomiting, and abdominal cramps. The label of pesticide shows that it has a high content of arsenic. Select the reaction which is affected by arsenic in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
G-3-P to 1,3 BPG

Arsenate poisoning

  • Arsenate inhibits the Glyceraldehyde-3-P dehydrogenase As a result, instead of G-3-P to 1,3 BPG, 1-arseno-3-PG will be formed.
  • But glycolysis continues even in the presence of arsenite but with no net ATP production.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No.166

questions.stem: The young lady of 24-year-old age in the second trimester of pregnancy reported to the gynecologist for a routine examination. In a routine laboratory test, mild hyperglycemia was detected after the intake of oral glucose in an oral glucose tolerance test. It was found that the lady had hyperglycemia more severe than gestational diabetes and not as severe as insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus. The pregnant lady was diagnosed as suffering from Maturity Onset Diabetes of the Young (MODY-2). Select the gene responsible for MODY-2?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glucokinase gene
  • Maturity Onset Diabetes of the Young or MODY is a mild type of hyperglycemia that develops in young women, generally below the age of 25 years. Its prevalence is mostly 1 to 2% in the population.
  • It is important to distinguish MODY-2 from the population who is suffering from type-1 and type-2 diabetes mellitus. Mutation in the Glucokinase gene is responsible for the Maturity Onset Diabetes of the Young. Mutation in hexokinase gene-1 is responsible for hemolytic anemia.
